title: Border Patrol agents kill VA nurse Alex Pretti during Minneapolis protest
description_short: Border Patrol agents kill VA nurse Alex Pretti during Minneapolis protest
description_medium: On Jan. 24, 2026, VA intensive-care nurse Alex Pretti was shot and killed by federal border agents during Minneapolis protests tied to Operation Metro Surge. DHS later told Congress that two federal officers fired their weapons, and reporting said Pretti had been filming and helping a pepper-sprayed woman when agents moved in. The killing became a flashpoint for protests demanding an end to the ICE surge.
description_long: Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse at a veterans’ hospital, was shot and killed by federal officers during protests in Minneapolis on January 24, 2026. The Hennepin County medical examiner classified the death as a homicide caused by multiple gunshot wounds and said he had been shot by law-enforcement officers. USA Today reported that a Department of Homeland Security account said two federal officers fired their weapons; that report did not establish that bullets from both officers struck Pretti. Pretti’s killing became a focal point of demonstrations against the federal immigration operation in Minneapolis. Reporting said he had been filming and had moved to help a woman who had been pepper-sprayed before officers approached him. The circumstances and use of force remained under investigation in the reporting cited here. The medical examiner’s finding describes the manner of death, not whether the shooting was legally justified. The account should keep those questions separate while documenting the confirmed fatal shooting, the agency’s report that two officers fired, and the public response that followed.

title: Trump Vodka Discontinued After Poor Demand (2011)
description_short: Trump Vodka Discontinued After Poor Demand (2011)
description_medium: Trump Vodka launched as a premium licensed brand in 2006 but failed to sustain demand. Reporting says domestic sales ended in 2011 after weak volume and high production costs, including expensive glass bottles and gold-leaf labels. The product joined a wider portfolio of Trump-branded ventures that often relied on licensing and marketing.
description_long: Trump Vodka was introduced in 2006 with premium branding and the slogan “Success Distilled.” Trump predicted it would compete with leading high-end vodkas, but sales remained small. Bloomberg’s retrospective reported that the brand sold only 184 cases in the three months before Halloween 2010, roughly two cases a day, and said the Dutch distillery that produced it went bankrupt that year. A separate account from the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette said domestic sales were discontinued in 2011 because of weak demand and high production costs. The packaging, including a premium glass bottle and gold-leaf label, added expense that made the product harder to price competitively. The venture illustrates the difference between brand recognition and sustained consumer demand: prominent marketing did not translate into enough purchases to keep the domestic product viable. Trump Vodka was part of a broader licensing strategy in which his name was placed on consumer products without requiring him to operate every part of the business. The available reports document the sales shortfall and discontinuation, rather than establishing that every Trump-branded business followed the same pattern.

title: Trump Repeatedly Promises to Invoke Insurrection Act Against Americans
description_short: Trump Repeatedly Promises to Invoke Insurrection Act Against Americans
description_medium: Throughout 2023, Donald Trump repeatedly promised to invoke the Insurrection Act on his first day back in office to deploy active-duty military against American citizens for mass deportations and to suppress protests. Retired senior military officers publicly warned such actions would be illegal and unconstitutional. General Mark Milley called Trump a fascist to the core in interviews published in 2023. The promises alarmed Pentagon officials and military lawyers who began preparing responses to potential illegal orders.

title: Trump Guts EPA, Halts Enforcement of Environmental Laws
description_short: Trump Guts EPA, Halts Enforcement of Environmental Laws
description_medium: In February 2025, the Trump EPA announced it would halt enforcement of dozens of major environmental regulations, including Clean Air Act provisions and clean water rules. Hundreds of EPA scientists and enforcement staff were fired or placed on administrative leave. Pending enforcement actions against corporate polluters were dropped. The administration framed rollbacks as eliminating regulatory burden, but environmental groups documented immediate upticks in pollution violations going unaddressed. The changes represented the most sweeping reversal of environmental enforcement in the agency's 55-year history.
description_long: CNN reported that EPA staff responsible for the industrialized Midwest were told to pause enforcement against oil and gas companies. The report focused on Region 5, which oversees six states, and said staff were no longer issuing notices of violation or information requests to fossil-fuel companies suspected of pollution. Such notices are a prerequisite for bringing certain alleged violations to court, so the pause could limit enforcement activity while it remained in place. CNN based its account on multiple sources familiar with the regional office; it did not report that all EPA enforcement nationwide had stopped. A separate CNN article described the administration’s announced plan to roll back more than a dozen pollution rules, including standards involving power plants, vehicles, soot, mercury, and coal ash. Those regulatory changes required a process and were not all completed when announced. Together, the reports document a broad deregulatory agenda and a specific regional enforcement pause, but they describe different actions and stages. This entry’s broad title should not be read as proof that every environmental law ceased to be enforced or that all announced rollbacks had already taken effect.
